posts.title: Here is the part of the Form 700 nobody tells you about.
posts.caption: Here is the part of the Form 700 nobody tells you about. A filing is not carved in stone. If an official finds a mistake, or something was left out, they file an amendment, and the amendment is public too. The original stays on the record, the correction sits beside it, and anyone can read both. That is how a disclosure system earns trust, not by pretending the first draft was perfect, but by showing the fix in the open. So when you read a Form 700, check the amendments. The correction often tells you more than the filing. Full breakdown in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: Form 700 Is Due April 1. Mark the Calendar.
posts.caption: Every public official in California lives by one date, and it is April first. That is when the annual Form 700 is due, the financial disclosure that shows what an official owns, earns, and owes. Take office and the clock is different: thirty days from the day you are sworn in. Leave office and you get thirty days the other way. Candidates file when they file their nomination papers. The calendar is the whole point. A disclosure filed late is a disclosure hidden, even for a week, so mark the date and then go read the filing. Full breakdown in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: Illegally Fired, episode 362: Thursday Check, Week Twenty-Six
posts.caption: Illegally Fired, episode 362: Thursday Check, Week Twenty-Six. Wednesday pinned the first line to the wall, and Thursday holds the week to it. The count stands where the week can see it, twenty-five books sealed on the shelf, and the open lines named beside them, each with the date it comes due. A line on the wall means every move gets measured against it, and a move that does not match the line gets named on the spot, not filed away for later. The sealed lines stay sealed, and the open lines stay where everyone can read them, with the week answering to the wall all day long. Twenty-six weeks running, and Thursday holds the week to the wall. General information, not legal advice. posts.title: California, Explained: The School Board.
posts.caption: California, Explained: The School Board. Five people, elected by their neighbors, hold the most local power in public education. The board sets the policy, approves the budget, and hires the superintendent — all in public, with an agenda posted before the meeting. The board does not run the schools day to day. That is the superintendent's job. The board's job is direction, and the direction shows up in the votes. Read the agenda, watch the vote, and know the five names before election day. | California, Explained. Full breakdown in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: ILLEGALLY FIRED: A LETTER TO MUHSD
posts.caption:
209connect Newsletter — Read Aloud | Edition #6 — November 25, 2025
ILLEGALLY FIRED: A LETTER TO MUHSD

The letter, read aloud. Full text below.

Two-oh-nine Connect. November twenty-fifth, twenty twenty-five. Illegally Fired: a letter to M U H S D. I forced disclosure, and now they are being legally forced to respond.

To Brett Nickelson, Rebecca Shelton, and Superintendent Peterson. Regarding determination response, pattern of delay.

Mr. Nickelson, I am in receipt of your determination letter dated today. This is simply an acknowledgement that we have received your letter further delaying the release of records to now December 19, 2025, after a 14 day extension. I must also note, that after ignoring my first two simple requests, you intelligently acknowledged my final legal request for public information. And in each of those instances, the legal deadlines were barely met. One even seemed to be scheduled on a district holiday day off.

While I acknowledge your production of the personnel file, I note with significant concern your request to delay the production of electronic communications, Request number 5, until December 19, 2025. This represents a substantial delay beyond the statutory timeframe, particularly given that electronic records are easily searchable and retrievable.

It also does not escape my notice that the District is using the exact same playbook as August 2023. Back then, as confirmed by Ms. Fonseca's email on August 28, 2023, I was removed simply for sending emails to Superintendent Peterson regarding Substitute Pay Equity, clearly documented in the paperwork you just now sent.

In 2023, I chalked it up as miscommunication. I let this slide. In 2025, I am demanding one because things have became clear to me.

You cited Deliberative Process Privilege. Be advised: discussing how to silence an employee for advocating for fair pay in 2023, or exercising free speech in 2025, is not a deliberation, it is actually a liability.

Furthermore, your letter cites the Deliberative Process Privilege, Government Code, section seventy-nine twenty-seven point seven-oh-five, as a potential basis for withholding these records.

Let this email serve as notice: the public interest in disclosing whether a public agency yielded to external political pressure and doxing campaigns to terminate an employee far outweighs the District's interest in keeping those deliberations secret. Deliberative Process cannot be used to shield the District from accountability regarding potential violations of First Amendment rights or discriminatory practices.

I expect the records to be produced on or before December 19, 2025, with minimal redactions. I will be scrutinizing the exemption log closely. I look forward to receiving the unredacted communications. The clock is ticking.

Yours truly, David Sicairos, Office of the Sovereign Architect.

That letter went out November 25th, 2025. The records were due December 19th. This is Two-oh-nine Connect, the newsletter, read aloud. The full letter is in the show notes, and the next edition is coming.

posts.title: ILLEGALLY FIRED: Keep the Ledger
posts.caption:
KEEP THE LEDGER.

After the firing, I stopped arguing from memory. Every meeting got a date, every name got written down, and every letter went into the file in order. A story people can dismiss is not the same as a record people have to answer.

Leaders do not win by remembering harder. They win by writing it down while it is fresh. Date it, name who was in the room, and keep the paper.

posts.title: THE PAPER TRAIL.
posts.caption:
THE PAPER TRAIL.

The paper trail starts with two dates. September 11, 2025, a public post names him and his workplace. September 18, the district fires him, and the letter gives no reason. Between those dates, the record shows calls flooding the district office. What the file does not show matters too. No documented warning, no documented process, and no reason in writing. That gap is not a verdict. It is the question the records still have to answer, and the audit keeps asking it.

His account, told through documents only. Follow 209Connect California.

posts.title: RENAMED AND REFILED.
posts.caption:
RENAMED AND REFILED.

They did not answer the record. They renamed it. A file that asked hard questions came back with a softer title and a new folder, and the questions inside did not change. Renaming a file does not resolve it. It only makes it harder to find. Keep your own copy, date it, and file it where you can find it again.

His account, told through documents. Daylight is the fix for a quiet file. What will you file today?

Full record in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio. Follow @castlecaliforniacounterintel.

posts.title: SHOW UP ANYWAY.
posts.caption:
SHOW UP ANYWAY.

On the days motivation is gone, the practice is simple. You do not need a perfect workout. You need a steady one. Walk, lift, stretch, rest, then repeat tomorrow. The win is not how hard one day feels. The win is how many days you keep the promise. Boring works because boring repeats.

Today, keep it simple, keep it honest, and show up anyway.
